summary: This change adds release jobs that publish @cipherstash/auth (the wrapper plus six native platform packages) to npm and stack-auth/stack-profile to crates.io. It also adds an auth flag to the release gate. Merged as it stands, it is inert. The npm auth jobs need gate.outputs.auth == 'true' and a successful gate, which cannot both hold while the seven auth packages are frozen. The crates job runs only once the @cipherstash/auth freeze entry is removed. CI tests that check this gating ran and passed. The material risk comes later, at arming (PR E). The publishing path only checks that each platform binary is present; the architecture and smoke checks are only in a manual preflight that has not run in the supplied CI. One freeze entry also arms both the npm and crates.io lines. For releases today, merging this alone changes little: the release job also waits on a skipped publish-auth, and release-plz.yml triggers on more paths.

behaviour_changes.description: The release gate reports a third flag, auth, for unpublished @cipherstash/auth* packages and stops counting them as js. At head js is only logged, so the js change does not alter any job's behaviour.

release.yml gains jobs that build the auth native binaries, publish all seven auth packages to npm with OIDC provenance, and then tag and create a GitHub release. They run only when gate.outputs.auth == 'true' and the gate succeeded. While the auth packages are frozen those two conditions cannot both hold, so the jobs are inert.
The JS release job now also waits on publish-auth. When auth is in scope, changeset publish runs only after publish-auth succeeds.
release-plz.yml gains a crates.io publish job for stack-auth and stack-profile. Removing @cipherstash/auth from FROZEN_PUBLISHERS arms it, so the npm and crates.io lines share one switch.

release-plz.yml now also triggers on changes to the root Cargo workspace, Cargo.lock, packages/stack-auth, packages/stack-profile, release-plz.toml and cliff.toml. Those pushes also run the already-armed EQL release job.
Changesets puts the seven auth packages in one fixed version group. Each auth manifest gains repository.directory, which npm provenance needs.
A new workflow_dispatch dry run, auth-preflight.yml, builds all seven tarballs, checks binary architectures and smoke-installs linux-x64-gnu. It has no publish credentials.

failure_scenarios.title: First armed run publishes an auth platform package whose binary is wrong or unloadable
failure_scenarios.trigger: PR E, or any later edit, removes the @cipherstash/auth entries from FROZEN_PUBLISHERS while an auth version bump is on main, and auth-preflight was not run on that exact ref.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: On the publishing path, _build-auth-artifacts.yml only checks that each platform tarball has the right name and contains a stack-auth-node.<platform>.node file. The architecture and libc checks and the install smoke test exist only in the manual auth-preflight.yml, which release.yml neither calls nor requires. This build workflow has not run in any supplied CI, so its first real execution may be a live publish. The cross-target legs are the likeliest to produce a binary that is present but wrong: darwin-x64 on an arm64 macOS runner, and linux-x64-musl on a glibc host with musl-tools.
failure_scenarios.consequence: A platform package is published with a binary that does not load because of the wrong architecture or libc. Customers on that platform get a load failure from @cipherstash/auth. An npm version cannot be republished, so the fix needs a new release.

existing_verification.description: Static tests on the build workflow: --js false, the clean-tree check, the wrapper packed with pnpm, and every platform built
The architecture, libc and smoke checks in auth-preflight.yml (manual dispatch only)

missing_verification: No supplied CI run executes _build-auth-artifacts.yml or auth-preflight.yml
No binary other than linux-x64-gnu is load-tested on its own platform
The publishing path has no architecture check
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Before PR E arms the line, run auth-preflight on the ref to be released. Better, have release.yml run the same file/readelf architecture checks on auth-tarballs before publish-auth, so the guard does not depend on someone remembering a manual step.

failure_scenarios.title: One switch arms npm auth publishing and crates.io publishing together
failure_scenarios.trigger: The @cipherstash/auth entries are removed from FROZEN_PUBLISHERS, either on purpose in PR E or as a side effect of another edit.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: crates-armed reads the @cipherstash/auth entry because no crate has its own entry, so removing it arms release-crates as well as the npm auth jobs. Unlike the npm line, the crates line has no frozen-bytes check. release-plz release publishes any root-workspace crate whose in-tree version is not on crates.io. Its preflight only decides whether to import the GPG key.
failure_scenarios.consequence: If crates.io lacks the in-tree stack-auth/stack-profile version 0.42.3, or a hand bump is already on main, arming publishes the imported source to crates.io at once, and the publish is irreversible. If crates.io Trusted Publishing has not been repointed yet, the job fails loudly instead.

existing_verification.description: eql-pipeline-armed tests check that the crates line keys on @cipherstash/auth and gates exactly release-crates. The release-plz-root-config test checks that only the two crates release.

missing_verification: I could not check whether crates.io has stack-auth/stack-profile 0.42.3 (no network)
No test checks that arming the crates line is a no-op when the versions are already published
failure_scenarios.mitigation: In PR E, before deleting the entry, confirm that crates.io already has the in-tree versions and that Trusted Publishing names cipherstash/stack and release-plz.yml. Consider a separate arming key for the crates line.

failure_scenarios.title: A failing auth build holds every JS release on main
failure_scenarios.trigger: After arming, an auth version is unpublished and auth-artifacts or publish-auth fails, for example after a runner image change, a cross-compile failure, or with no npm trusted publisher configured.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The release job requires publish-auth to succeed whenever gate.outputs.auth == 'true'. That same job opens and updates the Version Packages PR and runs changeset publish for every other package.
failure_scenarios.consequence: The release fails closed. Nothing else publishes (stack, stash, protect-ffi) and the Version Packages PR is not updated until auth is fixed or the freeze is restored. The failure is loud and recoverable.

existing_verification.description: A release-gate test asserts that the release job waits for publish-auth

missing_verification: No dry run of the full release.yml auth path
failure_scenarios.mitigation: This fail-closed behaviour is intended. Run auth-preflight before arming so the first armed run is unlikely to fail, and document the revert path: restore the freeze entries.

failure_scenarios.title: Wider release-plz path filter starts the armed EQL publish job on root Cargo changes
failure_scenarios.trigger: A push to main touches only Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml or the stack-* crates while an eql-bindings version bump on main is unpublished.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The push path filter applies to the whole workflow, not to each job. The EQL release job is armed, so it now also runs on these paths.
failure_scenarios.consequence: The EQL release can publish on a push unrelated to EQL. It runs the same guarded, idempotent release that the next EQL push would run, so mainly the timing changes. With nothing pending, the extra runs do nothing.

failure_scenarios.mitigation: Accept this, or move the stack-* line into its own workflow file if separate triggers matter. Note that crates.io binds the publisher to the filename.

Before PR E, confirm that crates.io already has the in-tree stack-auth/stack-profile versions, and that the crates.io and npm trusted publishers name cipherstash/stack and the right workflow files.

evidence.claim: All seven @cipherstash/auth packages are in FROZEN_PUBLISHERS at head. This map is the single switch for both the npm auth jobs and the crates.io job.
classify() now emits a separate `auth` flag for names starting with @cipherstash/auth and excludes them from `js`.
The gate writes the ffi/auth/js outputs, then exits 1 on any blocker. CHECK A blocks a frozen package whose committed version is not on npm.

auth-artifacts and publish-auth run only when classify mode is production and gate.outputs.auth == 'true'. Neither uses always(), so a failed gate skips them. publish-auth has id-token: write and runs npm publish --provenance per tarball, platform packages before the wrapper.
The release job (changeset publish and the Version Packages PR) now needs publish-auth. It requires gate success, and publish-auth success whenever gate.outputs.auth is 'true'.

crates-armed runs `node scripts/eql-pipeline-armed.mjs crates`. release-crates (contents, pull-requests and id-token write; GPG key; release-plz release on the root Cargo.toml) runs only when armed == 'true'.
The `crates` line keys on the @cipherstash/auth entry of FROZEN_PUBLISHERS. An unknown line name throws.

The release-plz.yml push paths now also include packages/stack-auth/**, packages/stack-profile/**, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, release-plz.toml and cliff.toml. These trigger the whole workflow, including the existing EQL `release` job.

The EQL release job is gated on eql-armed. @cipherstash/eql is not in FROZEN_PUBLISHERS at head, so the EQL line is armed. Its preflight short-circuits when the eql-bindings version is already on crates.io.
The root release-plz.toml releases only stack-auth and stack-profile, in one version group, and marks the other seven members release = false.

The root workspace has nine members. stack-kms, stack-encrypt, stack-encrypt-derive, stack-guest-abi and the three node/wasm binding crates are publish = false. stack-auth and stack-profile are at 0.42.3.
In the release build, each platform leg checks only that the tarball name matches and that stack-auth-node.<platform>.node is present. This path has no architecture, libc or load check.
The wrapper job checks that the exports and files paths are in the tarball, that the six platform peers equal the wrapper version, and that there are seven distinct tarballs.

auth-preflight.yml (workflow_dispatch only) checks each binary's architecture with `file` and its glibc/musl linkage. It installs and smoke-tests only the wrapper with linux-x64-gnu. release.yml does not call or require it.

ci.json for the head commit: 17 checks succeeded and 12 were skipped. The successes include Run Tests (Node 22), Run Tests (Node 24), actionlint (release workflows) and Verify no caching in release workflows. No check run for _build-auth-artifacts.yml or auth-preflight.yml appears.
The Run Tests (Node ...) job runs `pnpm run release:gate` and `pnpm run test:scripts`. test:scripts executes scripts/__tests__/*.test.mjs.

New or extended tests assert that: the gate flags auth and not js; the auth jobs run only on the gate and hold the release; crates-armed keys on @cipherstash/auth and gates exactly release-crates; release-plz.toml names every workspace member; the napi build uses --js false; and the wrapper is packed with pnpm.

The PR says every new publishing job stays inert until PR E removes the @cipherstash/auth freeze, which switches the npm and crates.io jobs on together. It reports one surviving mutation (the EXPECTED_DISPATCHABLE entry).
The changesets config gains a fixed group for the seven auth packages.
